## Historical audit: S0355

**Scope.** Student trajectory, chunk 1 of 2 only. All citations below refer to source S0355, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H06/selection/bw_0017/1/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and renders are named in the trace but are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1, `model_request` | The requested goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a 512 × 267 indoor photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, objects, materials and occlusions. The student’s inventory interpreted it as an industrial hall; that semantic interpretation is not independent image verification. |
| First build — lines 3–4, H `model_response` and `execute` | The program constructed multiple named assets: hall, platform and two stairs, four machines, ducts, tank and conveyors, with child parts such as rails, legs and rollers. It set colored material finishes, a camera and lights. Hierarchy and coordinates show intended connections and poses, not that parts visibly connect or match the photograph; no texture map is evidenced. |
| Validation — lines 6–10, build/render completion, `execution_result`, `select` | Build and render completed successfully and step 1 was selected. The printed conveyor landmark was (0.072, 0.705) against the student’s estimated (0.08, 0.85); these are approximate point projections, not contour or visibility measurements. |
| Revision — lines 11–14, H request and response, step 2 `execute` | After receiving the reference, render and execution output, H reported roof exterior, undersized equipment and sparse foreground, and hypothesized an outside, too-high camera. It executed a lower, closer camera, extended the shell and added a conveyor run. These are student observations and diagnosis, not independently verified defects. |
| Projection trade-off — line 19, step 2 `execution_result` | Build and render succeeded. The machine-top projection improved against its estimate, while window, tank and conveyor point errors worsened; the conveyor point moved to x = −0.066. This establishes a numerical trade-off, not overall visual improvement. Step 2 was selected (line 20). |
| Third revision — lines 21–24, H request and response, `execute` | H reported dark windows, sparse foreground and simple machinery; it added a platform extension, third stair, lower housing and foreground frames, lengthened the tank, changed glazing emission and lighting, and implemented camera/tank projection checks. The step 3 build and render completed with return code 0 (lines 25–28); their projection output and resulting image are not included in this chunk. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No separate teacher diagnosis or proposed update is visible. The task and runner supplied procedural guidance and render feedback; H’s subsequent revisions demonstrate use of that feedback, not receipt of a teacher intervention. H generated and revised code itself; its three recorded sessions show no tool calls (lines 2, 12 and 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** There is technical success for three builds/renders, but overall reconstruction correctness and final selection are **unknown**. No timeout or empty patch is observed. The student’s claims about roof, brightness, density and part connections remain unverified without the images; lighting versus material causes and the effectiveness of the third revision remain hypotheses. A transferable lesson from the recorded checks is that improving one landmark can worsen others; the particular camera, tank and conveyor choices are scene-specific.
